note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: PEEU hindsight task alignment yields better OOD web planning than atomic or coarse tasks

nodes.name: Small MLLMs plan weakly
nodes.description: Small open-source MLLMs suit web agents for cost and privacy but have weak planning ability and limited cross-website generalization.

nodes.name: Coarse high-level tasks are misaligned
nodes.description: Coarse high-level exploration tasks are misaligned with their trajectories (e.g., task requires over 4.5 stars but trajectory reaches 4 stars) and lack stricter constraints that only real exploration of a partially observable site can reveal.

nodes.name: PEEU method
nodes.description: PEEU has two stages: planning tree exploration (the model autonomously sets goals from a homepage and explores to build an exploration tree) and planning experience utilization (extract atomic experiences from before/after observations, then aggregate them into hindsight-aligned, more strictly constrained high-level tasks).

nodes.name: Training beats retrieval for small models
nodes.description: Retrieval-based prompting with the same experiences fails for small models (7B Atomic/Trajectory-Prompt 3.7% vs base 7.8%; 3B 0.0%), while PEEU-GRPO training reaches 19.9% (7B) and 11.1% (3B).

nodes.name: PEEU beats coarse and atomic baselines
nodes.description: With 2k trajectories on Qwen2.5-VL-7B, PEEU-SFT reaches 30.6% overall on unseen websites versus 19.0% for Coarse-SFT and 21.7% for Atomic-SFT, and exceeds Qwen2.5-VL-32B (22.7%).

nodes.name: Gains hold across scales and data
nodes.description: PEEU's gains hold across 3B and 7B models and 0.1k and 2k trajectories, e.g., 7B 0.1k PEEU-GRPO 19.9% vs Atomic-GRPO 10.0%.

nodes.name: TDHAF framework
nodes.description: The Task Decomposition Hierarchical Analysis Framework defines low, mid and high task levels and studies ID bottom-up, ID top-down and OOD multi-level generalization.

nodes.name: Low-level mastery does not transfer up
nodes.description: Models trained on low-level tasks reach 80.5% (3B) and 89.6% (7B) Step SR on low-level tests but only 9.1% and 18.8% on in-domain high-level tests.

nodes.name: High-level training generalizes down in-domain
nodes.description: Coverage of good in-domain multi-level generalization is 44.8% (3B) and 51.9% (7B) when trained on high-level tasks, versus 3.2% and 9.1% for low-level training.

nodes.name: High-level training generalizes better OOD
nodes.description: Out-of-domain coverage is 33.8% (3B) and 37.8% (7B) for high-level training, versus 18.9% and 25.7% for low-level training.

isolated_nodes.name: Training setup
isolated_nodes.description: Experiments use Qwen2.5-VL-3B/7B-Instruct, GPT-4o for exploration and experience summarization (max 15 steps), SFT and GRPO training, and evaluate on seven unseen WebVoyager websites with identical trajectory scales for all methods.

isolated_nodes.name: Atomic-level training limits generalization
isolated_nodes.description: Atomic-level task training limits cross-website generalization; Atomic-SFT/GRPO trails PEEU for both 3B and 7B models across data regimes.

isolated_nodes.name: Prior atomic-task approaches unproven for high-level tasks
isolated_nodes.description: Existing methods train on atomic tasks (click, type, scroll) from before/after observation changes, but it was unclear whether this generalizes to high-level tasks.

isolated_nodes.name: Step SR metric
isolated_nodes.description: Step SR counts a single-step prediction as correct only if the element Id, action type and action value all match the ground truth.

isolated_nodes.name: Allrecipes training source
isolated_nodes.description: Training uses either 0.1k trajectories from Allrecipes or 2k trajectories from a previously unseen website, and testing uses seven additional websites excluded from training.

structural_reasoning: PEEU's hindsight alignment is tested on unseen websites; TDHAF analysis explains why high-level tasks generalize better than low-level ones.
